Restrict an LD matrix to chromosome or LD-block structure

convertLD.Rd

Takes an LD matrix (dense or sparse, for one chromosome or several) and sets to zero every entry between two SNPs on different chromosomes (to = "chr") or in different LD blocks (to = "block"), returning the same kind of object as calLD. Entries inside a chromosome or block are kept unchanged, so the result is exactly the chromosome-wise or block-wise LD that calLD would compute from the same genotypes.

Usage

convertLD(LD, SNP.info, to = c("block", "chr"), LDB = NULL)

Arguments

LD

A p x p symmetric LD matrix: a base matrix or a Matrix (for example the XtX of calLD).

SNP.info

A data.frame describing the rows of LD, in order, with columns CHR (numeric, 1 to 22) and BP. SNPs must be sorted by chromosome, then position, as calLD expects.

to

"block" (default) or "chr".

LDB

For to = "block", an m x 3 matrix of LD block boundaries (chr, start, stop) in the build of SNP.info$BP, with numeric chromosomes, as for calLD; for example getLDB() read with read.table(). Ignored for "chr".

Value

An object of class "LD": XtX (the restricted p x p dgCMatrix, dimnames kept), blk (0-based block start indices with the end marker p, as calLD; for "chr" one block per chromosome) and nz (seq_len(p): no column is dropped).

Details

The conversion only removes entries. It goes from a dense LD to chromosome LD to block LD, never back: LD between blocks that a panel does not store cannot be recovered. In particular, a panel shipped as blocks (for example the PRS-CS UK Biobank panels, see convertLDref) cannot be turned into chromosome LD or into a different block partition.

Keeping the diagonal blocks of a positive semidefinite matrix keeps it positive semidefinite (the block mask is itself positive semidefinite), so a valid LD matrix stays valid.

See also

calLD, getLDB, convertLDref

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ldb = read.table(getLDB("AFR", "hg38"), header = TRUE)
ldb[, 1] = as.numeric(sub("chr", "", ldb[, 1]))
dense = calLD(X_ref)                                # full LD
blk = convertLD(dense$XtX, SNP.info, to = "block", LDB = as.matrix(ldb))
chr = convertLD(dense$XtX, SNP.info, to = "chr")
} # }
